hard_failures.summary: The extension predicate that the C2 conclusion quantifies over is under-frozen relative to its own C0 sibling, so the exact class content depends on conventions the file does not fix.
sub_items: (a) Manifold category of M': extension_predicate clause (c) and topology.extension_topology say only 'connected 4-manifold', while the C0 sibling freezes 'SMOOTH (C-infinity) connected 4-manifold' with the accepted rationale that a merely topological M' cannot carry a classical Lorentzian tensor field (worker-16 F2b-16-03).

(b) Regularity of iota: F2a says only 'isometric embedding' and has no iota_regularity field; F2b freezes iota as a C-infinity isometric embedding and records that this removes the R2-04 ambiguity. With g' only C2, the pullback equality iota_* g = g'|iota(M) is not typed without a differentiability convention on iota.

(c) Clause (f): F2a requires only p in M' minus iota(M) with p in I^+(q;g'); F2b adds int(M' minus iota(M)) non-empty and p in int(...) after the accepted R2-major finding that the unqualified clause was escapable by extensions that add only boundary/dense-open points. That repair reasoning is not regularity-specific and was not propagated.
hard_failures.consequence: The admissible extension set E_C2 (hence the strength of 'no proper future C2 extension') is reader-dependent: the naive smooth-embedding reading and the literal reading give different classes. The frozen F0 taxonomy itself flags the embedding-versus-metric regularity subtlety as an unresolved definitional point that 'must be fixed by F2/L1' (research_map/formulation_taxonomy.yaml#0abb9ed8a961, AF-SCC-C0-VAC-GEN hypotheses.H4). F2b fixed it for C0; F2a did not.
hard_failures.minimal_repair: Freeze, in extension_predicate and topology.extension_topology, that M' is a smooth (C-infinity) 4-manifold carrying a C2 metric, that iota is a C2 isometric embedding (or C-infinity, matching the sibling), and add the interior-future requirement to clause (f). One sentence each; no class-semantics redesign.

findings.detail: provenance.no_status_claim says 'no assertion that this class is proved, refuted, or open; L1 owns the ledger', while known_status.status asserts open_problem and epistemic_status asserts open_problem twice. Two careful readers can disagree on whether the artifact claims a status. Suggested repair: replace the absolute prose with the ledger-owned phrasing used by the sibling ('no progress claim') or drop known_status.status.

'E(C0) entails E(C2)' reads as an entailment between extension SETS, which is backwards against implication_ledger.extension_class_containment (E_C2 subset E_C0); what holds is 'not E_C0 entails not E_C2' (C0-inextendibility entails C2-inextendibility). A reader following the set notation can invert the implication direction. Suggested repair: state it in words ('no C0 extension entails no C2 extension') as the sibling does.

The consistency evidence records the compared paths but not the sha256 of the compared bytes, so by itself it cannot detect that the compared F0 or supplement content changed after the check. The chain currently closes only because the schema separately declares/freezes those bytes. Suggested repair: record the measured hashes in the evidence JSON or bind it to FROZEN.
